previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted two days after discharge due to recurrent malignant hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia, and acute kidney injury in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He was treated with IV fluids, a new cycle of chemotherapy with bortezomib, dexamethasone, and cyclophosphamide, and insulin therapy for steroid-induced hyperglycemia. During his stay, he developed a cough, and a chest X-ray revealed a left mid-zone infiltrate consistent with pneumonia. He was initially started on azithromycin but switched to levofloxacin due to transaminitis. His calcium, renal function, and glucose levels stabilized, and he was discharged home on oral levofloxacin, insulin, and his baseline medications with close follow-up arranged in oncology, endocrinology, and urology.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital after you experienced fatigue, 
weakness, and shaking chills. You were found to have bacteria in 
your blood. We are not sure where the bacteria originated from, 
but because your port could be a source we decided to send you 
home to complete a 14-day course of an antibiotic called 
vancomycin.

While you were in the hospital we made changes in your insulin 
to manage your diabetes. While you were here, the insulin we 
gave you during the day made your blood sugar go low enough that 
you became sick and confused. After that happened, we decreased 
the amount of insulin you received at meal times so this 
wouldn't happen again. We will be giving you a new sliding scale 
that shows how much insulin to take during meals.

While you were here, you experienced pain on the left side of 
your groin. We took an ultrasound to see if there was a hernia 
or something else dangerous causing the pain, but we didn't find 
anything, and the pain went away on it's own.

While you were here we also noticed that you had a heart murmur. 
We took an ultrasound of your heart (an echocardiogram) to see 
if there was an infection, but everything looked good.

To treat your blood infection it is important that you complete 
two weeks of strong antibiotics (vancomycin). You completed one 
week in the hospital, but it is important to complete the second 
week at home so you don't get sick again. The antibiotics will 
go in through the port on your chest. A nurse ___ come to your 
home every day to administer these antibiotics. You will take 
the antibiotics every day until ___.

After you finish your antibiotics you will meet with your 
oncologist to discuss the next step in your chemotherapy. You 
will meet with Dr. ___ ___ on ___. Someone from 
the hospital will call you with the time of your appointment.

It was an privilege to help take part in your medical care.

We wish you the best,
Your ___ Care Team
